## Planning Summary for `#improve-readme`

### What already exists (and is good)
| File | Status |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | Clean, well-structured. Has two cross-links to `docs/manual.md`, a Quick Start, status table, and command overview. |
| `docs/manual.md` | Comprehensive — covers every command, file format, behaviour rules, Python API, and agent integration. |

### Gap analysis & subtask breakdown

#### README improvements

| Subtask | Bookmark | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Add `[>]` Deferred row to status table | `#readme-deferred-row` | The status table in README lists 6 statuses but omits `[>] Deferred`. The manual has it; README should match. |
| Add `qt show` and `qt list --verbose` to command overview | `#readme-show-verbose` | Both commands exist in the manual but are absent from the README's command summary table. |
| Add a "Why Quick Task?" features section | `#readme-why` | The README jumps straight to installation. A short bullet list of differentiators (plain-text, version-control-friendly, agent-ready, Python API) gives readers context and improves discoverability. |

#### `docs/manual.md` improvements

| Subtask | Bookmark | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Fix Project Structure — `USAGE.md` legacy reference | `#manual-project-structure` | The structure diagram lists `USAGE.md` as a legacy file. If it no longer exists this is misleading; the executor should check and remove or update the line. |
| Expand Python API section | `#manual-api-example` | The current example is a minimal stub. A fuller example showing error handling (`TaskNotFound`, ambiguous match) and the `save` pattern makes the API section actually useful. |
| Navigation footer / verify ToC anchor links | `#manual-toc-links` | A long document benefits from "↑ Back to top" section footers. Also worth verifying that auto-generated anchor slugs (e.g. `#subtasks--hierarchy`) match GitHub/PyPI rendering rules. |

### Execution order
All six subtasks are **independent** — the executor can tackle them in any order or in parallel. No subtask depends on the output of another.
